basis: Vertebral and rib ossification defects define disease; renal cysts and myelomeningocele each reported in 80-99%. Respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.
Inherited junctional skin blistering; oral mucosal blistering affects 1/2 reported patients, supporting gastrointestinal involvement with limited sampling.
Peripheral nerve sheath tumor involving the pleura; both neural origin and pleural location are defining.
Malignancy of precursor T lymphocytes; lymphoma mandates the immune mechanism axis. Mediastinal location alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Clonal dendritic-cell neoplasm; destructive bone lesions occur in approximately 80% and skin lesions in roughly 30-40% of children. Other organ damage is less common across the group.
Early-onset monogenic diabetes defines endocrine pancreatic dysfunction; neurologic or exocrine abnormalities belong to particular subtypes.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with visual loss; all supplied manifestations concern the eye.
In situ epithelial carcinoma confined to the gastric body.
Congenital skeletal muscle disease with atrophy and multiple joint contractures. Respiratory insufficiency does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy; weakness is neurogenic. Reported scoliosis and clubfoot affect fewer than 30%.
Transient neonatal hyperparathyroidism with abnormal skeletal mineralization; osteopenia occurs in 2/6 patients (~33%). Motor delay alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Intellectual disability, microcephaly and speech delay define the syndrome. Cardiac and skeletal malformations are occasional; external ear shape does not imply hearing damage.
Thymic epithelial tumor; thymus falls outside the listed axes. Associated myasthenia, red cell aplasia and hypogammaglobulinemia are separate diseases.
Ovarian epithelial tumor of a reproductive organ; no defining endocrine dysfunction or other qualifying organ involvement.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with speech delay and frequent seizures defines neurologic disease.
Inherited red-cell membrane potassium leak produces an in vitro artifact, not systemic hyperkalemia. Hypertension annotations do not establish direct vascular disease from this benign defect.
Childhood autoinflammatory periodic fever syndrome; recurrent fever alone does not establish lasting damage to another organ.
Organic aciduria defined by optic atrophy and choreoathetosis; visual degeneration and central motor dysfunction are core disease features.
Cerebellar malformation, hepatic fibrosis and coloboma define COACH; renal dysfunction with echogenic kidneys and raised creatinine occurs in 1/1. Hypertension omitted under the four-axis cap.
Immune-mediated recurrent inflammatory arthritis defines joint disease despite complete remission between attacks; progression to rheumatoid arthritis is a separate diagnosis.
Cerebellar neurodevelopmental disorder; contractures occur in 3/3 and ankle contractures in 5/5. Abnormal ERG (1/1) supports retinal dysfunction, though much visual impairment is cerebral.
Conjunctival adhesion extending onto the cornea; disease is confined to ocular structures.
VIP-secreting endocrine pancreatic neoplasm defines disease. Secretory diarrhea and electrolyte losses reflect hormone action; intrinsic bowel damage is not established.
Fibrosis directly affects the bile duct, which belongs to the hepatic axis; no specific immune cause is established.
Inherited nonsyndromic lens opacity; cataract occurs in 10/10 patients. Other reported manifestations also remain within the ocular axis.
